scenes.title: CNS LISE Cleanroom Bays
scenes.institution: Harvard University — Center for Nanoscale Systems
scenes.reference_notes: Official Cambridge LISE tour preview informs a selected three-bay/corridor subset. Historical CNS 2009 photolithography slide 33 provides actual AB-M and MJB4 photographs for separate exterior silhouettes. Internal bearings, rigid wafer clamps, motion drives and all dimensions are authored; no current inventory, measured floorplan or exact OEM reconstruction claim.
observed_cues: Official Cambridge LISE dollhouse preview shows long circulation corridors, numerous process bays and a yellow-lit cleanroom section.
Historical AB-M photograph: tall left cream illumination tower, sloping front, black folded shroud, central binocular head, wide base with angled gauge/switch panels and right articulated grip.
Historical MJB4 photograph: central rear light enclosure, binocular head, black crossed stage and separate black switch/display panels.
Both photographs show yellow-lit glazed cleanroom walls, repeated mullions and wall utilities.

task.name: Position an inert wafer for alignment inspection
task.description: Measured positioning of a rigidly retained inert wafer beneath the visible right objective axis, inspection and return. Source-bound control validates actual per-step clearances and measured pose; no lithography or focus model.
task.observable: Measured wafer center/objective projected-axis alignment, unobstructed ray to actual wafer, full operation states, collision coverage and physical return.
task.sample_attachment: Three visible clamp assumptions; wafer belongs to the X-stage rigid body, with no insertion or unclamping capability

layout_rationale: Selected three-bay subset with a continuous front corridor and distinct yellow lithography bay, following the facility preview rather than its full floorplan.
Open-frame alignment benches, vertically supported instrument heads, flanged chamber cabinets and estimated utilities supply recognizable cleanroom context.
Bay partitions, glazing, gowning storage, dimensions and device placements are authored estimates; no full facility scan was ingested.
The left-wall entry opens into a reserved corridor; process furniture stays within bays and clear of the 1 m doorway approach.
Primary AB-M-inspired and secondary MJB4-inspired exteriors remain separate historical instrument references; bay assignments and their coexistence in this layout are inferred.
limitations: Room dimensions and unseen placements are estimated from public images; no institution has validated this scene.

scenes.title: SMTC Campus Membrane Test Aisle
scenes.institution: Nanyang Technological University — Singapore Membrane Technology Centre
scenes.reference_notes: Inspected brochure page 3 shows six captioned views: analytical benches, industrial research aisle, membrane fabrication machines, pressure-retarded-osmosis apparatus and separate outdoor pilot facilities. These are multiple sites/zones, not one room. This is a selected reference-informed room subset; exact dimensions, topology and OEM geometry are not verified. The revised skid has connected frame feet, supported module saddles, curved service hoses, an open valve-stem bonnet and open carriage bearings. These hidden assemblies and all dimensions remain estimates; the separate PRO photograph supplies exterior cues only, not proof of this campus plumbing topology.
observed_cues: The official brochure separates an analytical room, campus industrial project area, membrane fabrication equipment and the outdoor Tuas pilot site.
The campus industrial area photograph shows open metal frames on both sides of a working aisle, pipes, computer terminals and suspended services.
Brochure device photograph shows membrane modules, white-ended components, fittings and black tubing.

scenes.title: Moreton Bay Research Aquarium
scenes.institution: The University of Queensland — Moreton Bay Research Station
scenes.reference_notes: Opened the facility page and visually inspected its aquarium photograph: a wet room with large circular tanks, yellow aquarium racks, plumbing and ceiling services. The text distinguishes the aquarium from four other laboratories. This is a selected reference-informed room subset; exact dimensions, topology and OEM geometry are not verified.
observed_cues: The official wet-lab photograph shows large circular tanks, yellow rack structures, overhead services and wet-room plumbing.
The official facility description lists two 4000 L tanks, one 10000 L tank and three racks each fitting twelve standard tanks.
The aquarium is a dedicated wet laboratory separate from the station's four other laboratory rooms.

equipment.role: Authored instrumented probe bridge over a reference-informed round tank

support.evidence: Integral authored feet/frame contacts floor; spatial dimensions estimated from references

task.name: Register and return an inert aquarium probe
task.description: Traverse the supported probe to an authored offset physical datum, lower through the static visual water level, geometrically observe the actual cap surface and return using the original drives. This fixture is not verified UQ hardware.
task.observable: Actual cap position relative to a fixed visible datum, clearances and measured return; no water sample or environmental measurement.

layout_rationale: Three large circular tanks and three yellow racks with twelve tank positions each establish the documented aquarium scale and characteristic arrangement.
Overhead feeds, return/sump context, water surfaces and a grated floor drain produce a distinct wet-room environment; the large-tank arrangement is estimated.
A motorized sampling bridge is added as an original mechanical-control fixture; it was not visible in the reference photograph and is not claimed as UQ hardware.
Only broad spatial cues can be recovered from the small published photograph; modeled tank geometry estimates nominal capacity classes without certifying fluid volume.
The left entry opens into the clear zone between the round tanks and rear rack wall; no desks or small tabletop-only aquarium substitute is used.
limitations: Room dimensions and unseen placements are estimated from public images; no institution has validated this scene.
Original procedural geometry, no downloaded OEM CAD and no source photographs packaged as textures.

The probe basin contains an estimated clear-water optical volume fitted to its authored floor and wall; other tanks retain approximate static display surfaces.
